human_tolerance.notes: Found in eastern deciduous and mixed forests, including wooded suburbs, and it can hold a home range in suburban oaks, where female ranges favour nesting sites over food.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Acorns and other mast are the staple winter food and are cached; squirrels nesting alone in winter save about 30 percent less energy than aggregated animals.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Two litters a year, of two to seven young; mothers wean the young 65 days after they are born. Cavities are used for breeding and, more intensively, in winter, while leaf nests serve mainly as summer refuges.

vocalizations.description: A soft, low murmuring chatter used between pairs at a nest or a feeding tree, most often heard after dark.

range.note: Eastern deciduous and mixed forests of North America. PanTHERIA gives a geographic range spanning latitudes 13.70 to 48.10 degrees, which reaches into the tropics, so it is wider than the eastern-United-States range described on Wikipedia; only the documented native country is listed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Climbs trees and glides between them on the patagium, descending at 30 to 40 degrees.

traits.flight.note: It does not truly fly: it glides on the patagium.

traits.nest_type.note: Uses tree cavities for breeding and, more intensively, in winter, and builds leaf-and-twig nests that serve mainly as summer refuges and resting sites; Cavity is chosen as the primary type.

traits.perching.note: Climbs and clings to trunks and branches but does not perch like a bird.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 63.87 g and PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 71.90 g.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Judgement band either side of the two-dataset mean; no allow-listed open source states the mass range for this species.

traits.length_m.note: PanTHERIA AdultHeadBodyLen_mm 127.98 mm. The schema wants nose to tail tip, and no allow-listed open source gives the tail length separately, so this value excludes the tail and the rendered model will be slightly short. PanTHERIA AdultForearmLen_mm is 40.71 mm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: PanTHERIA MaxLongevity_m 144 months converted to 12 years. This is a documented maximum rather than a typical lifespan.

traits.home_range_ha.note: PanTHERIA HomeRange_Indiv_km2 0.008785644 km2 converted to hectares.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Seed 40 mapped to 'seed', Diet-Fruit 30 to 'fruit', Diet-PlantO 30 to 'browse'. Wikipedia adds insects, buds, mushrooms, mycorrhizal fungi, carrion, bird eggs, nestlings and flowers; the trace animal share is omitted from the sourced fractions and noted under habitat.resources instead.

traits.social.note: PanTHERIA SocialGrpSize 1 (solitary). Wikipedia notes that wintering squirrels may nest in aggregates, which saves about 30 percent more energy, so the group size is held at 1 for the typical individual.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Activity-Nocturnal 1 (Crepuscular 0, Diurnal 0); Wikipedia states plainly that they are nocturnal.

traits.defense.note: Withdraws into a cavity or into a tree canopy rather than confronting a threat; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a strictly nocturnal animal that is easily approached while it feeds in suburban oaks, but it is a small animal with a strong startle response, so wariness is set mid-range.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value is 'Ar' (arboreal); a small ground share is retained because they come down to the ground to forage and to reach a nest, which is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts in tree cavities in winter and in leaf nests in summer.

habitat.resources.note: The three plant weights follow traits.diet; the invertebrate and mast weights are separate judgement entries, because acorns from red and white oak are named on Wikipedia as the expected food in a home range and no animal share is in the diet fractions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes the species as living in eastern deciduous or mixed forests and studies suburban home ranges in large red and white oaks, where females favour nesting sites over food. The flight distance is judgement; no allow-listed open source gives one.

seasonal.strategy.note: No open source states a migration or a fixed hibernation period for this species, so ActiveYearRound is used, with the seasonal change recorded as phases instead.

seasonal.phases.note: Two litters a year of two to seven young, weaning at 65 days, the summer leaf nest and winter cavity use, the mast cache and the winter energy saving from nesting in aggregates are from Wikipedia; the calendar windows are authored judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Weaning at 65 days after birth, from Wikipedia, and PanTHERIA WeaningAge_d 57.23; the 65-day figure is used. The 0.6 scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.chatter.note: No allow-listed open source describes this species' calls. The entry exists so the record can carry a nocturnal call at all, and its wording, time window and cooldown are authored, not sourced.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a grey-brown squirrel with a white underside and a furry patagium between the fore and hind limbs; the proportions and the patagium, eye and flat-tail boxes are authored judgement to render the gliding membrane.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. No program covers an arboreal nocturnal glider, but this program's gaits are parameterised, so flee_gait glide and forage_gait climb turn it into a tree-climbing, gliding animal; the rest window is left at the program's daytime default because the species is nocturnal. Climb has no pose in the quadruped body plan, so only glide is declared.
